title: Pop Culture Remix
description: A second round of simplified pop culture fun — iconic villains, classic game shows, famous fictional pairs, beloved sitcoms, legendary dances, and the best animated TV series ever made.

questions.question: Clad in black armor and breathing through a menacing mechanical respirator, this dark lord of the Sith was the chief villain of the original Star Wars trilogy — and delivered one of cinema's most shocking family revelations to Luke Skywalker.

Flying on a broomstick with an army of winged monkeys at her command, this green-faced villainess terrorized Dorothy, Toto, and their companions throughout the classic 1939 film, threatening them with the words: 'I'll get you, my pretty!'
questions.answer: Who is the Wicked Witch of the West?

questions.question: Brilliant, cultured, and utterly terrifying, this imprisoned cannibalistic psychiatrist — played by Anthony Hopkins in his Academy Award-winning performance — helped FBI agent Clarice Starling hunt a serial killer in the 1991 thriller 'The Silence of the Lambs.'

Portrayed by Josh Brolin through motion capture in 'Avengers: Infinity War,' this purple-skinned Marvel supervillain sought to collect all six Infinity Stones so he could wipe out half of all life in the universe with a single snap of his gloved fingers.

Louise Fletcher won the Academy Award for Best Actress for her chilling portrayal of this cold, manipulative head nurse who controls her psychiatric ward through fear and bureaucracy in the 1975 Best Picture winner 'One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest.'

Since 1983, host Pat Sajak and letter-turner Vanna White have presided over this beloved game show where contestants spin a large wheel and solve word puzzles — making it one of the longest-running programs in American TV history.

For 35 years, Bob Barker welcomed contestants from the studio audience with the iconic phrase 'Come on down!' on this CBS game show — and always closed each episode by reminding viewers to have their pets spayed or neutered.
questions.answer: What is The Price Is Right?

questions.question: When Steve Harvey took over as host in 2010, he brought his signature humor to this long-running game show where two families race to match the most popular answers to survey questions — accompanied by his dramatic 'Survey says!' reveal.

Regis Philbin's catchphrase 'Is that your final answer?' became a cultural phenomenon when this primetime quiz show launched in 1999, offering contestants the chance to win a million dollars by correctly answering fifteen multiple-choice questions.
questions.answer: What is Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?

questions.question: Alex Trebek hosted this beloved daily quiz program for 37 years until his death in 2020, presiding over a format that required contestants to always phrase their responses in the form of a question — a simple rule that became one of TV's most iconic traditions.

This lovable talking Great Dane and his lanky, perpetually hungry human pal have been solving spooky mysteries together since their animated debut in 1969 — typically fleeing in terror while their braver friends investigate the haunted location.

Created at MGM in 1940 by William Hanna and Joseph Barbera, this animated cat-and-mouse pair spent decades locked in a slapstick battle of chases and elaborate traps — producing some of the most beloved short cartoons of the 20th century.

In Ridley Scott's 1991 road film, Susan Sarandon and Geena Davis play these two best friends whose liberating weekend getaway spirals into a crime spree across the American Southwest — ending with one of cinema's most iconic final shots.

Through their CBS variety show in the early 1970s and their 1965 duet 'I Got You Babe,' this husband-and-wife musical pair became household names — even after their very public divorce in 1975, remaining pop culture icons independently.

Cartoonist Bill Watterson refused to ever license this mischievous six-year-old boy and his stuffed tiger for merchandise — and the beloved newspaper comic strip they starred in ran from 1985 to 1995, ending entirely on Watterson's own terms.

Amy Poehler plays the relentlessly optimistic Leslie Knope, the deputy director of the Parks Department in the fictional Indiana town of Pawnee, in this beloved NBC mockumentary comedy that ran from 2009 to 2015.

In this critically beloved Fox comedy, the wealthy Bluth family falls apart after patriarch George Sr. is arrested for fraud — leaving son Michael as the only sane family member, surrounded by oblivious relatives and perpetually repeating the line: 'I've made a huge mistake.'

Andy Samberg plays the goofy but surprisingly capable detective Jake Peralta at the 99th Precinct in this NBC cop comedy that also stars Terry Crews as the muscle-bound, yogurt-loving Sergeant Terry Jeffords.

This ABC mockumentary comedy followed three related Los Angeles families across 11 seasons from 2009 to 2020 — winning the Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series for its first five consecutive years.

At a fictional Colorado college, slacker ex-lawyer Jeff Winger is forced to assemble a study group with his eclectic classmates — including the movie-obsessed Abed Nadir — in this cult NBC sitcom celebrated for rapid-fire meta-humor and the devoted fan rallying cry: 'Six seasons and a movie.'

Village People's 1978 disco anthem became iconic not just for its catchy melody but for the crowd participation it inspired — audiences raising their arms to spell out the title letters Y, M, C, and A overhead in unison.

When this South Korean pop star's 2012 music video went viral, the world instantly mimicked his exaggerated 'horse-riding' dance — and the song became the first YouTube video in history to surpass one billion views.

This catchy 1993 song by Spanish duo Los Del Rio spread across the world by 1996, inspiring a simple arm-and-hip dance that became unavoidable at weddings, school dances, and sporting events throughout the late 1990s.

Wearing his trademark shiny parachute pants, this Oakland-born rapper declared 'Hammertime!' in his 1990 hit — and his signature slide-and-shuffle dance moves became the defining dance of early 1990s pop culture.

In her 1990 hit named after a style of expressive, pose-focused dancing that originated in New York City's underground Black and Latino ballroom scene, this pop icon instructed fans to 'strike a pose' and declared that 'beauty's where you find it.'

Four foul-mouthed elementary school kids — Cartman, Kyle, Stan, and the perpetually dying Kenny — tackle satirical real-world topics in the fictional Colorado mountain town that shares its name with this long-running Comedy Central animated series.

Seth MacFarlane created this Fox animated comedy set in Quahog, Rhode Island, starring the bumbling Griffin family — including power-hungry baby Stewie and the family's philosophical talking dog Brian.

When delivery boy Philip J. Fry is accidentally cryogenically frozen on New Year's Eve 1999 and wakes up 1,000 years later in New New York, he joins a scrappy space delivery company in this Matt Groening-created animated comedy.

Straight-arrow Texan Hank Hill is passionate about two things — his family and 'propane and propane accessories' — in this Fox animated sitcom set in Arlen, Texas, created by Mike Judge, the same man behind 'Beavis and Butt-Head.'
questions.answer: What is King of the Hill?

questions.question: In this FX animated spy comedy, a narcissistic secret agent with a photographic memory for obscure trivia works for an agency run by his own cold, demanding mother — and is notorious for his rapid-fire wit and complete disregard for his colleagues' safety or personal feelings.
